aiProviderSettings.adminSubtitle: Sets the AI provider for all users in this organisation. API keys are managed server-side and never entered here.
aiProviderSettings.dataHandlingWarningBody: Case narrative text (Gross/Microscopic/Ancillary descriptions) is sent to whichever provider is configured here for real, live AI features (report generation, synoptic field suggestions, template assignment). Confirmed directly: no field on this app's own request templates structurally includes patient name, MRN, or date of birth — those are never automatically appended. This does not cover free text a pathologist types directly into a narrative field; avoid including direct patient identifiers there. Transit to the configured endpoint is TLS-encrypted; at-rest retention and any Business Associate Agreement are governed by that provider's own contract with your organisation, not by this application. Confirm a real BAA is in place before using a non-mock provider with real patient cases.
aiProviderSettings.dataHandlingWarningTitle: ⚠ Data handling — read before selecting a provider:
aiProviderSettings.demoModeBody: AI responses are instant and simulated. No API calls are made. Safe for offline demos and testing. Switch to a real provider before clinical use.
aiProviderSettings.devSubtitle: Local override for development and testing. Takes priority over org settings. Never use in production.

description.addendum: An addendum is new, additional information appended to a finalized report (e.g. IHC, molecular/FISH results, outside consultation) that does not change the original diagnostic text. The original report remains entirely untouched.
description.amendment: A Major Amendment is a diagnostic or clinical revision to a finalized report — staging, classification, or interpretation is changing. Requires a Clinical Notification Log.
description.correction: A Minor Amendment (correction) fixes an administrative or clerical error — a specimen label, a misspelled name — without changing the diagnosis. No clinical notification required, but the explanation below is still the required audit trail.
description.correctionWithNotification: A Minor Amendment (correction) fixes an administrative or clerical error — a specimen label, a misspelled name — without changing the diagnosis. Your organisation requires recording which clinician was notified, and the explanation below is the required audit trail.

billingTypeTriggerSection.subtitle: Which real clinical event releases each billing component to the outbound dispatch queue. TC (technical component) releases as soon as its own specimen's grossing work is done by default; 26 (professional) and Global both hold until the whole case signs out. This is the real, admin-configurable override the Outbound Billing & Charge Event Engine's own acceptance criteria calls for — leave a row on its default unless a real, specific reason requires releasing that component at a different real event. A facility with its own release timing can override just that site below; every other site keeps inheriting the enterprise-wide setting.
billingTypeTriggerSection.title: Charge Release Triggers

biopsyResectionCorrelationSection.subtitle: How long after a surgical biopsy a later resection for the same patient is looked for as a correlation candidate, and which date that window starts from. The default is 180 days from the biopsy’s collection. A resection matches when it is collected or received inside the window. Set it for the enterprise, for each jurisdiction, and for each facility; the most specific setting applies.
biopsyResectionCorrelationSection.title: Biopsy-to-resection correlation window

concordanceReviewSettingsSection.subtitle: Controls the automatic comparison of a preliminary finding (e.g. a frozen section diagnosis) against the corresponding final diagnosis, and the optional review screen shown at sign-out. The pathologist always makes the actual concordance determination — these settings control whether the system helps surface it, never whether the pathologist's own judgment is required. This is the org-wide default — individual performing labs can inherit it or define their own values on the Facility Configuration edit modal, and individual staff members can further override either setting for themselves, per the same real Enterprise → Facility → Staff cascade this app already uses for Cytology QC sampling rates.

lockReasons.addOnOrderContent: An add-on order is cut from chosen blocks and lists what is ordered.
lockReasons.amendmentNotification: A changed diagnosis must record which clinician was told and how (CAP, RCPath).
lockReasons.autopsyAuthority: Gross examination is blocked until the written order (medicolegal cases) or the consent grant (hospital-consented cases) is on file.
lockReasons.batchCustodyChange: Aborting a batch or completing it anyway changes its chain of custody, so the reason is recorded.
lockReasons.batchProtocol: A batch records the protocol it ran on.
lockReasons.batchStain: A cytology staining batch is defined by its stain.
lockReasons.billingAudit: A billing change after sign-out must record why, so the charge and credit can be audited.
lockReasons.billingCodeCorrection: The correction bills the new code, so it needs a code that differs from the one being corrected.
lockReasons.biopsyArray: An array puts two or more specimens in one labelled cassette.
lockReasons.bodyReleaseCustody: Chain of custody: a body release must record who received the body and who released it.
lockReasons.cassetteReprintReason: Reprinting a cassette label needs a reason for duplicate-label and traceability records.
lockReasons.cisoeaMatrix: CISOE-A scores every axis independently; the result cannot be computed with any axis missing.
lockReasons.coldChainRecord: An acknowledged temperature excursion needs a note for the cold-chain record.
lockReasons.controlTraceability: A control well records its lot and expiry, so an out-of-date control can’t run.
lockReasons.correlationRecord: A correlation record needs both the histology diagnosis and the outcome to be usable in QA reporting.
lockReasons.criticalResult: Critical results must record who was told, how, and by whom (CLIA).
lockReasons.criticalResultDirect: A critical result is expected to go to the operating surgeon directly; any exception is recorded with its reason.
lockReasons.decalTiming: The decalcification timer counts down from the target duration.
lockReasons.deckPlacement: The instrument reads tubes by deck position, so the rack's instrument and slot must be known.
lockReasons.delegationRouting: Decides who the case or report goes to.
lockReasons.discordanceRecord: A frozen section that differs from the final diagnosis must be classified and explained (CAP, ISO 15189).
lockReasons.externalAddress: A secure email needs a recipient address.
lockReasons.facilityIdentity: A facility is identified by name on orders, reports and labels.
lockReasons.facilityRouting: Inbound HL7 orders are matched to a facility by its assigning authority, so it is required and must be unique.
lockReasons.fixationCompliance: CAP/ASCO biomarker guidance requires documented fixation timing before sign-out, or a confirmed exception.
lockReasons.holdAccountability: A hold stops work on the case, so placing or releasing one records why.
lockReasons.interfaceRouting: Once an interface is set up, messages cannot be routed without it.
lockReasons.intraopMergeTarget: A session is merged into exactly one case.
lockReasons.intraopReporting: The session records the operating surgeon. The frozen result may be given to the surgeon or an authorized member of the surgical team; who received it is recorded with the report.
lockReasons.materialTraceability: Changes to blocks and slides must be traceable: what changed and why (ISO 15189).
lockReasons.messageContent: A message with no text says nothing.
lockReasons.messageRouting: A message can't be sent without someone to send it to.
lockReasons.molecularRunRecord: A molecular run records the assay and the instrument it ran on.
lockReasons.orderingProvider: Laboratory regulations require the name of the person who ordered the test.
lockReasons.patientIdentification: Identifies the patient; laboratory standards require at least two identifiers.
lockReasons.pieceCountVerification: The observed piece count is compared with the count recorded at grossing; a mismatch raises a Tissue Discrepancy.
lockReasons.preAnalyticCompliance: Accreditation standards (ISO 15189, CAP/CLIA and equivalents) require collection and receipt dates, or a justified administrative override.
lockReasons.quickGrossGate: Touch prep and frozen sections are logged only after the specimen's Quick Gross.
lockReasons.rackIdentity: The rack is tracked through extraction by its identifier.
lockReasons.rackTraceability: A reusable rack is tracked by its ID.
lockReasons.readBack: A read-back of the patient identifiers and diagnosis is mandatory.
lockReasons.retentionHold: A retention hold stops material being disposed of, so placing or releasing one records why.
lockReasons.retrospectiveOutcome: A retrospective review without an outcome is not a review; the outcome is what the lookback records.
lockReasons.revisionRecord: Laboratory standards require every change to a signed-out report to record what changed and why.
lockReasons.routing: Decides where the case is routed and billed.
lockReasons.sampleMapping: Every tube on the rack must be linked to its sample, so each result can be traced back to the patient.
lockReasons.scannerInstrument: A slide sent for scanning is queued for a named scanner, so the scan can be matched back to the slide.
lockReasons.screeningResult: The primary interpretation is the screening result itself; a review cannot be saved without one.
lockReasons.sendOutRouting: A send-out without a reference lab leaves gaps in the courier and tracking logs.
lockReasons.slideChangeReason: Reprinting or cancelling a printed slide needs a reason for duplicate-label and traceability records.
lockReasons.slideOrder: A slide order without a stain can’t be cut or labelled.
lockReasons.specimen: A case needs at least one described specimen.
lockReasons.specimenDescription: Every specimen needs a description; it appears on the report.
lockReasons.specimenIdentity: Identifies the specimen on labels, blocks and the report.
lockReasons.staffAccess: What a staff member can do comes from their roles, so at least one is needed.
lockReasons.staffIdentity: A staff member is identified by name on cases, reports and the audit trail.
lockReasons.supersedeRecord: Superseding a run keeps the reason on both runs’ records.
lockReasons.verbalReportRecord: The record must show who received the result and their role.
lockReasons.wellTraceability: A patient well must name its specimen, so the result can be traced back to it.

modifierDictionarySection.subtitle: The reference list of CPT modifiers this app can attach to a billing code — the two-digit or two-letter suffixes (e.g. -26 Professional Component, -TC Technical Component, -59 Distinct Procedural Service) that tell a payer how a procedure was actually performed or billed. Referenced from the Billing Dictionary's own "Modifiers Commonly Associated" field as an informational guide for whoever is coding a case — PathScribe does not currently validate or auto-append a modifier onto a resolved charge (see the Limitations section of the Billing Capacity Review). The active version's descriptions are synthetic placeholders until a real, licensed admin imports their own real AMA modifier text below, using their own real license — PathScribe never embeds or redistributes that real, copyrighted text itself. A single entry can also be corrected directly (Edit, below) without a full re-upload — like every change here, it goes through the same real Four-Eyes approval process before it takes effect.

runtimeConfigError.help: Your IT team or ForMedrixAI support can correct config.json on the web server; reload this page afterwards. The settings are described in the deployment guide (RUNTIME_CONFIG.md).
runtimeConfigError.intro: This deployment's configuration file (config.json) has the problems below. PathScribe won't start until they're fixed, so it never runs with the wrong settings.

problems.ADDRESS_NOT_FROM_SERVER: The server can't set an address. Put it in config.json, so the site's security policy allows it.
problems.API_SERVER_IN_DEMO_BUILD: This is a demonstration build. It can't connect to a PathScribe server, so that its demonstration accounts never reach real data. Install a server build.
problems.API_SERVER_REQUIRED: This build needs the address of the PathScribe server, and none is set.
problems.INVALID_URL: This must be a web address, or a path on this site starting with /.
problems.NOT_AN_OBJECT: config.json must be a list of settings and their values (a JSON object).
problems.NOT_FROM_SERVER: Only config.json or the build may set this (sign-in, the instance role, which jobs the server runs and similar settings stay with the site). Remove it from the server's /api/config.
problems.NOT_HTTPS: This address must use https (plain http is allowed only to this computer, in a development build).
problems.NOT_IN_DEMO_BUILD: A demonstration build can't use this: it must never reach a real server, and it is never "production". Install a server build.
problems.NOT_TEXT: This setting must be text, a number, or true or false.
problems.NOT_THIS_SITE: This path leads to another site. Use a path on this site, or an https address.

header.title: Validation Studies

howItWorks.betaNote: Every model a study can be scoped to starts as <beta>Beta</beta> — advisory, never the org default, zero cases processed against real data — until a study like this one confirms it. A required field an AI model suggested a value for still has to be explicitly confirmed or overridden by a pathologist before a case can be finalized, regardless of how confident the model claims to be; nothing here relies on the AI's own accuracy claim as a substitute for that.
howItWorks.exampleIntro: Say Metro General Hospital wants to know if a new AI model is ready for their breast core biopsies.
howItWorks.footer: The Dashboard tab shows every active study's live progress toward its targets; the Reports tab is where finished studies' graded outcomes live.
howItWorks.intro: A validation study measures whether a specific AI model's suggestions are trustworthy enough for a specific facility, physician, or report template — before relying on it for real reporting decisions. Every study goes through the same six stages, shown as its status: Draft → Pending Approval → Approved → Active → Closed → Reported.
howItWorks.step1: Get the model. An admin gets notified — today, an email from ForMedrixAI — that a new model has been published following ForMedrixAI's own internal regression testing. From this screen's "New Study" form, Browse the ForMedrixAI store and download it; it lands in your system as Beta, never the default, with zero cases processed yet.
howItWorks.step2: Create the study (Draft). Scope it — the model you just downloaded, facility: Metro General, template: Breast Core Biopsy — and set your targets, e.g. 90% AI-suggestion acceptance rate and a maximum 15% edit ratio (how much pathologists end up changing).
howItWorks.step3: Submit for Review (Pending Approval). A second pathologist or admin reviews the study's scope and targets before it can start collecting real data.
howItWorks.step4: Record Approval (Approved → Active). Once approved, the study goes live — every matching report during the study period is scored against the targets, still fully advisory the whole time.
howItWorks.step5: Close the study. After enough cases (the Dashboard tab tracks this live), close it — this locks in the final numbers.
howItWorks.step6: Report. The grade is computed automatically: PASS if both targets are met, CONDITIONAL PASS if close but not quite there, or FURTHER REVIEW if performance fell short — each with the specific numbers behind it, exportable from the Reports tab. A PASS is what makes it reasonable for an admin to later consider setting this model as the facility's default, in the Models screen — this study is the evidence for that decision, not the model's own published benchmark.
